title: Strive Bitcoin Holdings Reach 35,595 BTC As Wall Street Raises Price Target 27%
summary: TL;DR: TD Cowen reportedly raised its Strive share-price target from $44 to $56 after the Bitcoin treasury company expanded its holdings to 35,595 BTC. Strive is also seeking financing through a substantial preferred-share offering. Bitcoin treasury company Strive is attracting fresh attention from Wall Street after a rapid buying programme took its reported holdings to 35,595 BTC. TD Cowen analysts increased their share-price target on Strive from $44 to $56 in an October 16 research update, pointing to the pace of the company’s Bitcoin acquisitions. The company has accumulated thousands of BTC in a matter of weeks, considerably exceeding some earlier analyst expectations. A Growing Treasury Needs Funding Strive’s strategy depends on raising capital and acquiring additional Bitcoin. Its announced purchases have positioned it among the larger corporate holders, though still far behind Strategy. The firm also announced pricing for a substantial preferred stock offering. Seven million shares at $90 each would generate approximately $630 million in gross proceeds before expenses, assuming completion on the announced terms. Such financing can raise cash without the immediate dilution associated with issuing common shares, but preferred dividends create their own ongoing costs. Strive has repeatedly expanded its Bitcoin holdings, including a previously reported purchase that lifted its treasury above 26,000 BTC. Bitcoin Per Share Is The Real Test A rising total BTC balance does not automatically mean existing shareholders benefit if the company simultaneously expands its share count or adds expensive financing obligations. For that reason, investors must assess Bitcoin holdings alongside the capital structure supporting them. TD Cowen’s higher target signals optimism about Strive’s execution, but remains an analyst opinion rather than a guaranteed future price. The company’s next financing and treasury disclosures will show whether it can keep increasing Bitcoin exposure on terms that make economic sense for shareholders. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Pantera Leads $10 Million Fission Funding Round To Solve Tokenized Fund Liquidity Problem
summary: TL;DR: Tokenization infrastructure firm Fission has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Pantera Capital. It wants to make it easier for eligible investors to sell tokenized private-market holdings without waiting for traditional fund redemption periods. The tokenization industry has spent years promising faster transfers of financial assets. Fission now wants to solve a more difficult problem: what happens when an investor wants their money back? The financial technology company announced on October 15 that it had raised $10 million in a round led by Pantera Capital, with participation from Circle Ventures and other investors. Its business focuses on liquidity for tokenized alternative investments, including private funds that are traditionally difficult to sell quickly. A Token Is Not The Same As A Buyer Representing ownership of a fund on a blockchain may make recordkeeping and transfers more efficient. It does not automatically create a liquid market. A private credit or private equity fund can still have transfer restrictions, limited redemption windows and few willing buyers. Fission is developing infrastructure to provide secondary-market liquidity for qualifying interests. Some transactions can be completed rapidly when liquidity is available, but that should not be confused with a guaranteed right to sell every asset instantly at full value. The company’s approach complements the industry’s wider interest in tokenized institutional investment products. The Next Stage Of Tokenization Investors increasingly want to know how tokenized assets can be financed, transferred and redeemed, not simply how they are issued. Fission plans to use the money to extend its infrastructure and support more asset managers. Pantera’s investment suggests that solving practical market problems may be at least as commercially significant as launching another blockchain-based security. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Strategy Declares Daily STRC Dividends As Saylor Targets $100 Share Price
summary: TL;DR: Strategy has conditionally declared daily STRC preferred-stock dividends for November 2026. The new cadence remains subject to shareholder approval and is intended to make the security more attractive to investors. Strategy is proposing another adjustment to the financing instruments supporting its Bitcoin treasury business, this time seeking approval to pay dividends on its STRC preferred stock every day. In an October 16 filing, the company outlined conditional daily dividend record dates for November. The announced rate was equivalent to approximately 12% annually, or $1 per preferred share for the month. The plan depends on amendments that shareholders are due to consider at an October 28 meeting. A Different Way To Attract Capital STRC, also known as Stretch, is a variable-rate preferred security developed as part of Strategy’s effort to finance Bitcoin purchases. Its appeal to investors is linked to recurring income and the company’s attempts to keep the share price close to its $100 reference level. More frequent distributions could reduce the time between earning and receiving a dividend. That does not automatically increase the total amount paid or guarantee daily compounding. Strategy has already used STRC-related financing to expand its Bitcoin holdings. The Costs Still Matter Preferred financing can raise money without immediately issuing more common shares, but it creates dividend obligations that require ongoing management. Those costs become particularly important during prolonged weakness in the Bitcoin market. If shareholders approve the changes and other conditions are met, the new STRC dividend schedule is expected to begin in November. Otherwise, existing arrangements will remain in place. For investors, the vote offers another indication of how sophisticated Strategy’s capital structure has become as its Bitcoin treasury grows. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Circle Reveals $819 Million USDC Payouts As Stablecoin Economics Come Under Scrutiny
summary: TL;DR: Circle says it generated roughly $1.4 billion in first-half 2026 revenue while spending $819 million on distribution partners and related costs. The disclosure highlights the expense of building a widely used stablecoin payment network. Circle’s USDC business is generating substantial revenue, but its latest disclosures show how much of that income is needed to support distribution and infrastructure. The stablecoin issuer reported approximately $1.4 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026. It said around $819 million went to partners and transaction-related costs, while another $473 million supported operational, compliance and technology spending. That leaves a much smaller proportion of revenue as retained profit than the headline size of USDC might suggest. The Economics Of A Digital Dollar Circle holds reserves backing USDC in cash and highly liquid financial instruments. Those assets can produce interest income, creating an important revenue stream for the issuer. But USDC’s usefulness depends on its presence across exchanges, wallets, payment services and other financial applications. Those distribution arrangements can be expensive. Coinbase is among Circle’s most important commercial partners, reflecting its role in making the stablecoin accessible to users. As NewsBTC has previously explained, USDC aims to maintain its value against the dollar while remaining transferable across supported networks. Competition Raises The Stakes New stablecoin issuers and conventional financial institutions are entering the market. They will compete not only on the reliability of their reserves but also on distribution, redemption and cost. Circle’s revenue also depends partly on interest rates. Lower yields on reserves could compress income even if USDC’s circulation remains relatively strong. The latest figures reveal an important part of the stablecoin business: issuing the digital dollar may be only the first step. The partners enabling people to use it can command a considerable share of the economic value. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Charles Schwab Opens Bitcoin And Ethereum Transfers As Crypto Rollout Expands
summary: TL;DR: Charles Schwab is expanding its direct Bitcoin and Ethereum services, including phased external wallet transfers. The move brings digital asset ownership further into the company’s conventional brokerage experience. Charles Schwab is moving its cryptocurrency service closer to the features customers expect from a dedicated digital asset platform. The brokerage has been rolling out direct Bitcoin and Ethereum trading to eligible clients, and its latest account documentation explains how approved customers can transfer supported assets to and from external wallets. For Schwab, that is a meaningful step beyond providing market exposure inside an investment account. Buying Crypto Is Only The Beginning Brokerage customers increasingly want to decide whether to hold digital assets with a financial institution or move them to another approved custody arrangement. Schwab’s transfer functionality is being introduced in phases. Users must meet identity verification requirements and may encounter security checks and waiting periods for approved wallet addresses. The platform also continues to distinguish cryptocurrency from conventional insured bank deposits. The value of Bitcoin and Ethereum is not protected by FDIC insurance merely because the assets are held through a Schwab service. As NewsBTC reported when Schwab introduced direct crypto trading, the rollout has been deliberately gradual. Traditional Brokerages Become Serious Rivals Schwab already has millions of brokerage relationships and well-established infrastructure. Adding cryptocurrency ownership makes those relationships increasingly valuable in a market where digital asset exchanges are competing with conventional financial firms. The company has also discussed expanding its supported assets beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum. The wider trend is clear: investors are increasingly being offered cryptocurrency services through the same institutions they use for stocks and other financial products. The competitive question is no longer simply whether traditional brokerages will support cryptocurrency. It is how much of the customer experience they intend to control. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Giants Feature In $210 Million Political Donations Report As Regulatory Scrutiny Grows
summary: TL;DR: An October 8 Public Citizen report links corporations and individuals benefiting from cancelled federal enforcement actions to approximately $210.5 million in donations and pledges to Trump-aligned political committees. Major cryptocurrency companies feature among the reported contributors. A report examining corporate political donations and changes to federal enforcement has placed several major cryptocurrency businesses under renewed public scrutiny. Consumer advocacy organisation Public Citizen said companies and individuals connected to beneficiaries of cancelled or curtailed enforcement actions had contributed or pledged roughly $210.5 million to Trump-aligned political committees. The research, originally published October 8, includes cryptocurrency firms such as Crypto.com and Gemini. It should not be described as a brand-new October 16 investigation. The Crypto Industry’s Political Spending According to the report, Crypto.com-associated contributions included $35 million to MAGA Inc. and another $2 million to a separate Trump-aligned committee. Public Citizen also examined contributions involving Gemini and the Winklevoss brothers, alongside regulatory matters affecting the exchange. The watchdog argues that the scale of political spending deserves attention, particularly where companies also benefit from changes in how government agencies pursue enforcement. But political contributions are not proof of an illegal arrangement. The report does not establish that the named donors purchased specific regulatory decisions. A Broader Political Debate The cryptocurrency industry has become increasingly involved in Washington, advocating for clearer legislation and a more predictable business environment. NewsBTC has previously reported on substantial cryptocurrency political contributions, part of a larger push to influence rules affecting exchanges, stablecoins and token issuers. Supporters of those efforts argue that previous regulation created unnecessary uncertainty. Critics say large corporate donors may enjoy disproportionate access to policymakers. Public Citizen’s findings add to that debate while leaving the central legal distinction intact: correlation between donations and enforcement outcomes does not establish corruption. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million Funding Round At $1 Billion Valuation
summary: TL;DR: Binance.US is reportedly seeking up to $100 million from private investors at a proposed valuation of approximately $1 billion. The financing discussions come as the American exchange attempts to rebuild after several difficult years. Binance.US is reportedly pursuing a $100 million fundraising round as it seeks to strengthen its presence in the American cryptocurrency market. Bloomberg reported on October 15 that the exchange was discussing an investment at a valuation of approximately $1 billion. If completed on those terms, it would represent a sharp reduction from the $4.5 billion valuation attached to its 2022 funding round. The discussions have not been announced as a closed transaction, and the proposed figures could change. Rebuilding A Damaged Business Binance.US once competed aggressively for American cryptocurrency traders but faced major regulatory and operational difficulties. The Securities and Exchange Commission’s earlier proceedings complicated the company’s relationships with banks and other commercial partners. As NewsBTC covered at the time, those disputes included an emergency application involving assets connected to the platform. Conditions have since changed, with US regulators adopting a different approach to digital asset businesses. But a friendlier environment alone does not guarantee that customers return. Fresh funding could support compliance, technology development and new products, while giving Binance.US greater flexibility to compete with established exchanges and brokerages. What The Valuation Suggests A proposed $1 billion valuation is not itself a completed market transaction, but it is a reminder of how substantially expectations for cryptocurrency platforms have evolved since 2022. The next challenge for Binance.US will be demonstrating that investment capital can translate into stronger trading activity and sustainable growth. For now, the fundraising discussions show renewed ambition rather than a finished recovery. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Arbitrum Courts European Investors Managing €800 Billion With New Revenue Pitch
summary: TL;DR: Arbitrum representatives have presented the network’s infrastructure and revenue model to European financial institutions managing substantial assets. The meetings should not be confused with confirmed investment commitments to ARB. Arbitrum is increasingly pitching itself as a blockchain infrastructure business rather than simply another cryptocurrency ecosystem. During institutional meetings reported on October 16, representatives discussed the network’s commercial potential with European banks, wealth managers and other professional investors. The participating organisations were said to represent more than €800 billion in assets under management. That figure describes the institutions attending the presentations. It does not represent money invested in Arbitrum or its native token. Explaining The Business Behind The Blockchain The discussions placed particular emphasis on how blockchain infrastructure can earn fees through licensing, network services and support for financial applications. Research presented alongside WisdomTree material explored Arbitrum’s financial performance and the possibility of building sustainable revenue rather than relying on speculative token trading. Institutional projects using Arbitrum technology are one possible route toward such a model. They demonstrate how a financial business might adopt blockchain infrastructure without requiring its customers to trade ARB directly. Arbitrum’s community has also discussed new ways to generate revenue for its DAO treasury. Interest Is Not Adoption The meetings do not confirm that any participating bank has committed to deploy the technology, purchase tokens or establish a product. For Arbitrum, the next task is converting conversations into actual commercial integrations. Banks will demand clear answers about reliability, compliance, privacy and the economics of using blockchain rails. Still, the change in emphasis is notable. Blockchain companies increasingly want to be assessed on the value of the services they provide, not simply the price of their coins. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Grayscale Opens DeFi And AI Crypto Funds To Investors With Just $2,500
summary: TL;DR: Grayscale and investment platform Republic are offering three specialised crypto funds with minimum commitments starting at $2,500. The products remain restricted to eligible accredited investors. Grayscale is opening another route into sector-specific cryptocurrency investing, reducing the minimum commitment for selected private funds through a distribution partnership with Republic. The products focus on decentralised finance, artificial intelligence and blockchain data infrastructure. Eligible investors can gain exposure through managed vehicles rather than purchasing every underlying cryptocurrency themselves. The $2,500 entry level is significantly lower than the sums typically associated with institutional private placements, but the offering should not be mistaken for a mass-market retail investment product. Beyond Bitcoin And Ethereum Grayscale’s decentralised finance portfolio includes projects associated with lending, trading and other blockchain-based financial services. Its AI strategy covers networks involved in decentralised computing and related technology. The partnership illustrates how asset managers are packaging more specialised cryptocurrency themes for investors who already understand conventional investment products. Grayscale has separately explored staking-related changes to its Ethereum and Solana investment structures, reflecting its effort to develop products beyond straightforward token-price exposure. The Important Restrictions Participation in the Republic offering is limited to accredited investors under applicable US securities rules. Private investment products may impose selling restrictions, and their holdings can be considerably less liquid than publicly traded ETFs. The lower minimum also does nothing to eliminate the volatility of the cryptocurrencies inside each portfolio. Still, the arrangement provides another example of how traditional asset managers are attempting to make a wider variety of digital assets accessible through familiar investment structures. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Deutsche Bank Nears Bitcoin Custody Launch As Crypto Push Expands Beyond Europe
summary: TL;DR: Deutsche Bank is preparing to introduce institutional digital asset custody services, initially targeting professional clients in Germany. The planned platform is part of a wider effort to connect cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets to established banking infrastructure. Deutsche Bank is nearing the commercial launch of its institutional cryptocurrency custody business, another sign that major European lenders increasingly regard digital assets as part of mainstream financial services. Comments reported on October 16 indicated that the German banking giant expects to begin serving institutional customers within weeks. Its offering is intended to support assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum, using technology developed with Swiss digital asset infrastructure company Taurus. This is not a new retail cryptocurrency trading app. The initial market consists of businesses and professional investors with demanding custody and compliance requirements. Why Banks Are Entering Custody Holding cryptocurrency for institutional clients involves more than storing private keys. Banks must address asset segregation, operational controls, reporting, insurance arrangements and regulators’ expectations. The service would allow eligible institutions to interact with digital assets through a familiar banking relationship rather than exclusively relying on specialised cryptocurrency companies. Traditional finance is already developing related infrastructure. Projects involving blockchain settlement and tokenized deposits illustrate how established financial businesses are adapting their systems. The Longer-Term Opportunity Deutsche Bank has also discussed tokenized deposits, digital securities and possible expansion into Asian financial centres in 2027. These ambitions remain subject to regulatory approvals and operating arrangements. A planned launch should not be confused with an already operating global service. Nevertheless, the direction is clear. Rather than merely offering clients exposure to cryptocurrency prices, traditional banks increasingly want to provide the infrastructure through which digital assets are held, transferred and managed. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
